agent_response.summary: Candidate 4 shrinks the per-frequency loop to the linear algebra only. Matrix assembly runs as the full 101-frequency vmap at top level, as in the parent: the signal component updates, carrier connector scaling, sideband conjugation and noise-matrix update. The loop (k=1) now covers only the signal solve, the explicit A^H, the noise-weight solve, the noise-source einsum, the covariance solve and the noise ASD. It steps through rows of the assembled matrices and the broadcast detector selections. Candidate 3 (47cd6495, k=2) passed the official check and failed strict. Its gradient was bit-identical to candidate 2's, including index 161, and it was slower: first run 23.677 s, compile 12.39 s, warm median 10.53 s, RSS 7.47 GB. So chunk size does not affect the gradient drift; only the presence of the loop does. Nothing was run locally.
agent_response.hypothesis: The gradient drift is the same at every chunk size, so it most likely comes from the reverse code XLA compiles inside the loop body rather than from batch shape. The candidates are component-function gradients and assembly scatter transposes, compiled with different fusion or FMA contraction. If so, moving assembly out of the loop should restore strict agreement at index 161 while keeping the solve-side memory and cache benefit. If strict still fails identically, the drift is in the solve and transpose path inside the loop, and the operator cannot pass strict as built. Expected timing: some of candidate 1's forward and RSS gain is lost because assembly's ~0.9 GB intermediates come back. The first run should land between candidate 1 (22.08 s) and the parent (24.66 s). This is unmeasured.
agent_response.notes: The notes file has full results for candidates 1–3: SHAs, screen and full IDs, phases, memory and comparisons. Both hypotheses so far were rejected: carrier accumulation order (candidate 2) and degenerate batch size (candidate 3). The best official-only result is candidate 1 at 22.076 s. About 43 minutes remain. Next: if candidate 4 passes strict, it is the first validated value of the operator, with the loop scope recorded as an operator condition. If it fails identically, record that a solve-scoped loop changes reverse rounding beyond the strict tolerance. Then hand off with candidate 1 as the fastest official-only result and parent 6dc993a as the validated fallback.
